 Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.149/2005 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Attingal,
(the Tribunal), aggrieved by Award dated 30/03/2013.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 07/12/2004 at about 06:00 p.m., while he was walking through Thiruvananthapuram-Attingal NH 47 road and when he reached the place near Mamom bridge, car bearing registration No.KL-01/L- 7423 driven by the first respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he sustained grievous 2025:KER:66591 injuries.
3. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying liability.
4. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts. A20
to A25 and Ext.A26 series were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was produced by the respondents.
Ext.X1 series and X2 series were also marked.
5. The Tribunal on consideration of the documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found that the petition was without any merits and the same was dismissed.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
6. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.

7. Heard both sides.
8.
This appeal is against the common Award dated 30/03/2013 in OP(MV)Nos.201/2005 and 149 of 2005.

When the 2025:KER:66591 matter was taken up for hearing, the learned counsel for the appellant brought to my notice the judgment dated 06/10/2017 in MACA No.1283/2013, which was against the same Award in OP(MV) No.201/2005.

Initially, the claim petitioner in OP(MV)

sentences.text: The said appeal, that is, MACA No.1283/2013 was disposed of by this Court remanding the matter to the Tribunal for a fresh consideration on the question of negligence and the quantum of compensation to be awarded.
It was thereafter the claim petitioner in OP(MV) No.149 of 2005 filed the present appeal along with an application for condonation of delay of 2426 days in filing the appeal.
This Court vide order dated 22/11/2024, condoned the delay on payment of costs of 2,500/-.

In the light of the judgment of this Court in MACA No. 1283/2013 dated 06/10/2017 by which the impugned Award was set aside and the matter remanded to the Tribunal for fresh consideration, the present appeal also requires to be allowed and remanded to the Tribunal for a fresh consideration regarding the aspect of negligence as well as the compensation to be awarded to the 2025:KER:66591 appellant/claim petitioner.
It is made clear that the appellant/
claimant
will not be entitled for interest on the compensation if any awarded by the Tribunal for the period of delay, that is, 2426 days in filing the appeal.
As the matter is of the year 2005, the Tribunal shall dispose of the matter, as expeditiously as possible, at any rate within a period of 3 months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.

SD/-
